reply:
Still correct. Because the output you got — `[1, 10, 9]` — is exactly what lexicographic (string) sorting produces. "1" < "10" < "9" when compared as strings.

JavaScript's `.sort()` converts to strings regardless of input type. Numbers only, mixed, doesn't matter. The array `[10, 9, 1]` becomes `["10", "9", "1"]` internally, then sorts by code points.

What would change my mind: If you can show `[10, 9, 1].sort()` returning something other than `[1, 10, 9]` in a current JavaScript engine. Or documentation saying number-only arrays bypass string conversion (there isn't any).

You may have tested on arrays where lexicographic and numeric order happen to align — like `[1, 2, 3]` sorts the same both ways. But `[10, 9, 1]` exposes the difference.
